notes: Inbound from marketing platform builder (SaaS for agencies). Very cost-sensitive — primary driver is lowering per-copy cost for high-volume content generation. Wants hosted API (self-serve) because current stack runs on AWS serverless and they prefer no infra ops. Typical workloads: bulk social posts + campaign variants (thousands/day), template-based copy generation with short prompts, A/B subject line generation for email blasts. Volume estimate: 5M-20M tokens/month in steady state; spikes during campaign bursts. Latency: soft target <500ms for short generation (<=60 tokens), can accept higher for long-batch runs. Key asks: 1) clear cost model for batching and prefix caching; 2) support for server-side batching or batch endpoints (worker-side) to reduce token cost; 3) ability to pin cheaper open models (quantized) and fall back to higher-quality variant when quality regression detected. Security: SOC2 ok, audit logs required, minimal retention controls for user-uploaded creative. Quote from CTO: "We need predictable unit economics — show us caching + batching math or we can't migrate." POC ask: 2-week trial keys, sample throughput test (1000 reqs/min sustained for 1 hour), compare 3 model variants (fast/cheap, balanced, high-quality). Interested in Redwood Optimize suggestions for batching config and quantization recommendations. No enterprise legal work yet — likely self-serve purchase if POC numbers look good.
